archetype.name: Pocket Passer (accurate, sack-prone)
archetype.definition: A 36-year-old rhythm thrower who wins with accuracy and timing to the intermediate and deep levels from the pocket. He rarely creates with his legs and absorbs too many sacks when the first read isn't there.

report.headline: Seattle-era efficiency is back, but sacks and top defenses cap him
report.take:
Geno Smith in 2026 looks much more like the Seattle version than last year's Raiders version. His 2025 was the outlier of his recent career: -0.1 EPA per play, 6.75 yards per attempt, 17 interceptions. This year he is at 0.058 EPA per dropback, 7.62 yards per attempt and +2.8 CPOE. That sits close to his 2022-24 band and comfortably above the league-average quarterback, who is at -0.021 per dropback. The accuracy that made him a top-ten CPOE passer in Seattle never really left, and the efficiency has followed it back.

The engine is the ball thrown past ten yards. Throws of 10+ air yards have added 52.8 EPA, against 8.6 on everything shorter. On 34 deep attempts he is completing 15.9 points over expectation. Garrett Wilson, Adonai Mitchell and, on fewer targets, Omar Cooper Jr. are all producing well above average per target. The short game is ordinary, and the screen and behind-the-line work has been a net loss.

The numbers hide where drives die. On third down he has taken 14 sacks on 93 plays and averaged 8.3 yards to go, and those plays sum to -9.3 EPA. In the red zone he has taken 7 more sacks and completed only half his throws, though 7 touchdowns came out of it. His 38.4% pressure-to-sack rate and 9% sack rate ranks 39th. Part of that is the line, whose hit rate allowed ranks 29th. Part of it is him: he was at 35.5% in 2024 and 46.2% in 2025, so holding the ball is a trait. The sudden lack of interceptions, 3 all year after 11-plus in each full Seattle and Las Vegas season, is the number most likely to move.

The game log splits cleanly by opponent. Against defenses now ranked 24th or worse (TEN, DET, NE, MIA, LV) he was productive almost every week. Against Chicago, Cleveland and Kansas City, all top-ten, his passing EPA went negative each time. The 0-5 run is as much a 30th-ranked defense forcing shootouts as anything he did. The newest wrinkle is the ankle that cut his Buffalo game to 48% of snaps.

strengths.title: Wins downfield with accuracy
strengths.body: His value is concentrated beyond ten air yards, where his accuracy over expectation is far above his short-area numbers. It rests on timing and ball placement rather than arm talent. That mirrors his best Seattle years, so it should hold, though a 34-attempt deep sample will cool some.

strengths.title: Accuracy back to Seattle level
strengths.body: His CPOE is up 2.1 points on last season, and he sits 4 points over the qualifier average. He has posted +5 or better CPOE in three prior seasons, so this is his baseline returning rather than a hot streak. It keeps the offense on schedule on early downs.

strengths.title: Two receivers who convert targets
strengths.body: Wilson and Mitchell are both producing well above average per target. That gives him reliable outlets to the boundary, where his right-side throws carry 6 touchdowns and no interceptions. Cooper Jr. has been the big-play outlier on a small target count.

concerns.title: Sacks kill drives in key spots
concerns.body: He holds the ball 2.93 seconds, up from last year, and converts too much pressure into sacks. Third downs and red-zone trips are where it bites. A bad pass-blocking line feeds it, but his pressure-to-sack rate has been poor in three of the last four seasons. Expect it to persist.

concerns.title: Interception rate due to rise
concerns.body: He threw 17 interceptions last year and double digits in most full seasons. Now he has 3. Lower aggressiveness explains some of it, but his bad-throw rate is actually up 1.8 points. More picks should come, especially on deep shots, where 2 of the 3 already are.

concerns.title: Good defenses shut him down
concerns.body: Against top-ten defenses (Chicago, Cleveland, Kansas City) his passing EPA went negative each time. The last three games, with Kansas City and Buffalo in them, dragged his CPOE to roughly zero. At 36, with no running game of his own, he has little to fall back on when the timing game is taken away.

trend.note: His week-to-week results track the opponent more than any steady arc: strong against bottom-ten defenses, negative EPA against the top tier. The last three games went 0-3 with below-average efficiency, though the Las Vegas shootout inside that stretch was one of his best games.

nextGame.headline: Leaky deep defense helps; ankle, low total and slow pace don't
nextGame.body:
The Chargers' defense is mid-pack overall, 14th against the pass, but its profile lines up with his. They are stingy underneath and 30th in deep EPA allowed, so the downfield throws that drive his season should be there if he can set his feet. They hit quarterbacks often but rank 26th in sack rate. For a passer whose problem is turning pressure into sacks, that is a real break. Their WR1 numbers are mixed: they have held lead receivers under their averages, yet allow plenty per target. Their offense is the league's worst by EPA and runs far more than expected, which should keep the game close and possessions scarce. The 40.5 total reflects that.

Availability is the swing. Smith is questionable after Monday tests found nothing major, but he left Week 10 having played under half the snaps. A limited ankle hurts most on the play-extension and step-up throws his deep game depends on. Guard Dylan Parham, a regular starter, is questionable with a knee on a line already 29th in hit rate allowed. Cooper Jr., his most efficient target per throw, is questionable with an ankle. For the Chargers, interior lineman Justin Eboigbe and a few depth defenders were out for their Monday game; Eboigbe's absence would thin their interior rush slightly.

keyMatchups.title: His deep game vs their soft top
keyMatchups.body: Los Angeles allows 0.853 EPA on deep throws, among the worst in the league, while Smith's deep attempts are his most valuable plays. If he is healthy enough to drive the ball, this is where the Jets can steal points in a low-total game.

keyMatchups.title: Hits without sacks
keyMatchups.body: The Chargers get hits at the 8th-highest rate but finish sacks at one of the lowest. Against Smith's habit of absorbing sacks, that tendency matters more than usual. A depleted Jets interior with Parham doubtful could still tilt it the wrong way.

keyMatchups.title: Slow, run-heavy game script
keyMatchups.body: The Chargers' offense ranks last in EPA and passes well below expectation. That shortens games and should spare the Jets the chase scripts their defense usually creates. That is good for efficiency and a cap on his passing volume.

nextGame.watch: Whether he is attempting and hitting throws 20+ yards downfield early; if the ankle keeps him to checkdowns, his edge in this matchup disappears.

restOfSeason.body:
The foundation is sustainable. His accuracy and intermediate-to-deep efficiency match what he did for three years in Seattle, and Wilson and Mitchell give him dependable targets. Expect him to stay an above-average per-dropback passer against weak defenses and a below-average one against strong ones. The 0-5 slide owes more to a bottom-three defense than to his play. Volume should sit around 195-240 passing yards a game, with a team that doesn't pass much over expectation.

Two things will regress. His interception rate is far below anything in his career and should drift up, perhaps toward 0.4-0.8 a game. His deep completion rate over expectation is unlikely to stay this high on a modest sample. The sacks are not regression candidates: they are who he is behind this line, and around 2.3-3.2 a game is the realistic band. The ankle and the Jets' standing at the bottom of the standings are the wild cards for how many of the remaining games he actually finishes.
swingFactors: Offensive line health (Parham) and sack rate
Cooper Jr.'s availability as a downfield option

confidence.note: Ten starts with a clear profile, but the ankle is unresolved and the deep and interception numbers rest on small samples.
